artifacts.summary: Re-derives the 153-suite corpus, confirms instance A (memory axis) remains isolated and closed, fully diagnoses instance B (timing axis, test-four-tier-conflict.sh cases 5/6) and sandbox-validates a PATH-shimmed causal fix needing zero production-code changes, verifies the 2026-10-04 fixture-completeness roster is now clean except one stale-artifact issue (fixed), cites pre-existing causal-assertion exemplars for the convention doc, and reports four full-corpus-run failures as out-of-scope for separate owners.

memory_candidates.content: When a shell suite's retry/polling loop under test tracks elapsed time via a nominal counter (incrementing by the configured poll interval) rather than reading the real clock, a suite asserting on that loop's EXTERNALLY measured wall-clock time is really measuring sleep-time-plus-subprocess-forking-overhead, which balloons under CPU contention. Fix: PATH-shim the loop's `sleep` call with a fake that counts invocations instead of delaying, then assert the exact invocation count (budget_ms/poll_ms) as a deterministic causal invariant -- removes host-load dependency with zero production-code changes, since PATH-based interception of a bare (non-absolute-path) command is a legitimate external test seam.

A suite's "this run created no stray artifact at a live, shared, non-fixture filesystem path" check must be delta-based (compare existence before the suite starts vs. after it ends), not an absolute existence check -- a pre-existing or externally/concurrently-created artifact at that same path (e.g. from an unrelated process sharing the host) otherwise produces a false attribution of the artifact to the suite under test, and the failure may not reproduce in isolation.
